question.problem:
$T$ is a bijection $\,⟺\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \bbox[3pt,white,border: 2px solid Gainsboro]{\phantom{WW}}={R}^{n} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=n \\  & \bbox[3pt,white,border: 2px solid Gainsboro]{\phantom{WW}}=\{0\} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 
$\,⟺\,$  $T$ is invertible

Consider the equivalence above, where $T:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T.$ **From top to bottom**, which of the following should be placed into the blank spaces to make the statements true?

current_example.problem:
$\mathbf{T}$ is a bijection ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14152988/assets/f841907cd9bdc26a5cdd190204ff13b83a369821da1131f083762f464c450a1c.svg) 
$\qquad \Longleftrightarrow \qquad$  $T$ is invertible

Consider the equivalence above, where $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is a linear transformation whose standard matrix is $T.$ What should be placed into the blank space to make a true statement?
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that the *invertible matrix theorem* (in terms of linear transformations) states the following: 

 $\mathbf{T}$ is a bijection ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14152988/assets/8d693ea39cd9a76114e3e217f341319fb0ea7f3ad8384fd403f75fdbdb6b59f2.svg) 
$\qquad \Longleftrightarrow \qquad$  $T$ is invertible

Therefore, the missing expression is $\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T}).$
